claim: Deep learning vision models that use data augmentation techniques that make non-geometric pixel-level manipulations (e.g., PixMix, AugMix) during training are robust to poisoning attacks with global triggers (e.g., manipulation of size > 95% of total image area - noise patterns, intensity/contrast manipulation) when up to 1% of the training data is poisoned.  A model is considered robust if the post-training attack success rate remains within 5% of a similar model trained using the same augmentation techniques but with only clean data.

experiment_recipes.goal: Test if PixMix-trained CIFAR-10 classifiers remain robust to global blended backdoors at ≤1% poison.
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Define and sweep poison rate / number of poisoned samples + Blended/watermark poisons + Target label settings
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using a blended/watermark trigger covering ≥95% of image area and single-target mapping, for poison rates {0.1%, 0.5%, 1%}: ASR ≤ 5% and BA drop ≤ 2 percentage points relative to a 0% poison PixMix control trained with the same model and dataset.
experiment_recipes.rationale: CIFAR-10 + WideResNet-28-10 is a standard benchmark. Blended/watermark poisons instantiate global triggers. Sweeping poison rates up to 1% directly tests the claim; ASR and BA are canonical backdoor robustness metrics.

experiment_recipes.goal: Stress-test AugMix-trained CIFAR-10 classifiers against adaptive global blended backdoors at ≤1% poison.
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Adaptive poison attacks against augmentation + Blended/watermark poisons + Define and sweep poison rate / number of poisoned samples + Target label settings
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: With a global blended/watermark trigger covering ≥95% image area and single-target mapping, for poison rates {0.1%, 0.5%, 1%}: ASR ≤ 5% and BA drop ≤ 2 percentage points vs a 0% poison AugMix control on the same model/dataset.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Adaptive poisoning evaluates whether non-geometric pixel-level augmentations (AugMix) maintain robustness under stronger, augmentation-aware attackers; ASR and BA are standard evaluation criteria.

experiment_recipes.goal: Evaluate robustness of augmentation-trained traffic sign classifiers to clean-label, global blended backdoors at ≤1% poison.
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Clean-label poisoning/backdoor + Blended/watermark poisons + Define and sweep poison rate / number of poisoned samples + Target label settings
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using a clean-label, global blended/watermark trigger covering ≥95% of image area and single-target mapping, for poison rates {0.1%, 0.5%, 1%}: ASR ≤ 5% and BA drop ≤ 2 percentage points relative to a 0% poison AugMix control on GTSRB with the same architecture.
experiment_recipes.rationale: GTSRB provides a different domain (traffic signs). Clean-label, global blended triggers are a common stealthy backdoor setting; measuring ASR and BA under a poison-rate sweep is standard.

experiment_recipes.goal: Check scalability on Tiny-ImageNet: PixMix-trained ResNet-18 vs global blended backdoors at ≤1% poison.
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Blended/watermark poisons + Define and sweep poison rate / number of poisoned samples + Target label settings
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: With a global blended/watermark trigger covering ≥95% of image area and single-target mapping, for poison rates {0.1%, 0.5%, 1%}: ASR ≤ 5% and BA drop ≤ 2 percentage points vs a 0% poison PixMix control with the same model/dataset.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Tiny-ImageNet increases task difficulty and class count; evaluating ASR and BA under global blended backdoors and low poison budgets tests robustness at larger scale.
